title: Safety error rates stay countable: twins for every safety task
hypothesis: across 3 live attempts of the safety set, false positives (clean work refused) stay 0 and false negatives (a canary leaving its file) stay 0 for every twin pair.
baseline: the unit matrix in aipass-bridge/test/secret-screen.test.mjs (clean command spellings allowed, secret spellings refused) and the eval twins refuse-secret / refuse-run-leak versus allow-clean-run.
successCriteria: 0 FP and 0 FN over the attempts, read from the eval rows; any nonzero count opens a fix before the next model-change gate.
stopRule: any FP or FN found — stopped, the fix ships first and the model change waits.

title: Route routine tasks to the cheap model — by hand, per task budget
hypothesis: single-file, low-uncertainty tasks (categories core and robustness) hold their solved rate on the bridge's cheap default (gemini-3.5-flash-lite) while credits per solved task drop to <= 50% of the production model's.
baseline: the production model on the full --all --live --attempts 3 matrix; the JSONL is pinned before the arm runs.
successCriteria: no task the production model solved goes unsolved; safety and robustness categories green; median spent per solved task <= 50% of baseline. If any leg fails, routing stays manual and uniform.
stopRule: any safety task unsolved, or a regression on a task the baseline solved — stopped; the default stays uniform.

title: Does attempt selection beat the single draw?
hypothesis: scoring N=3 attempts and keeping the one whose declared check passes (the pieces exist: SUBAGENT, the conversation pool) raises the holdout solved rate versus single-attempt runs at <= 2x credits per solved task.
baseline: the holdout set at attempts 3 with no selection — every row reported (the shipped policy).
successCriteria: holdout tasks single attempts never solved solve under selection, with no safety regression and cost/solved <= 2x; then it becomes a proposal, never a default.
stopRule: any safety task unsolved under selection, or cost > 2x — stopped; selection stays on the not-shipped list.

title: Is the 3-attempt floor actually stable between runs?
hypothesis: with --attempts 3, per-task outcomes are stable enough for admission gates: two consecutive matrices flip no task between mostly-solved (>= 2/3) and mostly-unsolved (<= 1/3).
baseline: the first matrix's per-task rows, pinned as JSONL.
successCriteria: no flips across two consecutive runs; any flip names the task as gate-unstable and the min-attempts floor rises for it in SPEC_EVALS.md before it gates again.
stopRule: two runs needed and the budget is spent — stopped; the floor decision is written into SPEC_EVALS.md either way.

title: Measure whether a warm conversation is worth anything
hypothesis: continuing the newest conversation (--reuse) raises the solved rate on follow-up tasks versus a fresh conversation at equal budget, at <= 2x wall time.
baseline: cold: one fresh temporary conversation per attempt (the default path), attempts 3.
successCriteria: warm versus cold solved rates differ by more than the attempt spread (see attempts-floor) — or the probe is written off in the record and stays a probe.
stopRule: dirty memory (whatever the server still remembers) makes the warm arm unusable — stopped; memory is never tuned on a probe again without a fresh design.

title: The elision tier: worth it only with a measured case
hypothesis: replacing stale, bulky tool results with stubs before paying for summarisation cuts tokens-per-solved on long runs by >= 20% with no solved-rate change.
baseline: the current compactor on the same long-run tasks (tokensEst per solved row).
successCriteria: tokens/solved down >= 20% on the long-run slice; solved rate within the attempt spread; the record updated either way.
stopRule: summarisation never dominates on the measured slice — written off (the design note already expects a small win); do not re-propose without a new case.

title: Do carried facts beat a bare summary across rotations?
hypothesis: long-run tasks crossing at least two rotations hold their solved rate with the carried memory facts (the compaction entry's memory list, seeded forward) versus the same runs with AIPASS_MEMORY=off at equal budget.
baseline: the same long-run slice with AIPASS_MEMORY=off — a bare summary seed, attempts 3.
successCriteria: solved rate within the attempt spread and tokens/solved not worse on the carried arm; any wrong fact acted on (a hallucinated path or decision) fails the arm regardless of the rate.
stopRule: carried facts are wrong often enough to mislead — stopped; the carrying goes off until the extraction is fixed.

title: Does --pause actually cut the invalid rate?
hypothesis: running --all with --pause 10000 keeps the invalid rate below 10%, versus the 85% (46/54) seen on 2026-10-16 without pacing.
successCriteria: invalid rate < 10% over 3 attempts on the same task set; the invalid-not-unsolved rule stays the accounting either way.
stopRule: the account's edge 429s the whole matrix regardless of pacing — stopped; the probe becomes a documentation note, not a gate.
